uncited: *   **Output:** An L-block Covering (LBC) representing the Enhanced Volume Data Set (EVDS), consisting of a set of connected L-blocks and their hierarchical relationships.
An LB is an axis-aligned box containing voxel data.
A hierarchical structure storing connected LBs.
*   Apply a conservative labeling function to segment critical data.
*   Retain only the immediate predecessor ($Z$) in memory.
*   Focus on connected components in the extended volume data set.
Isolated vertices outside connected components may be retained as individual LBs.
*   **Noise Removal II (Isolated):** Eliminate small disconnected LBs.
*   Combine LBs to minimize header overhead.
*   **Time Complexity:** Real-time incremental generation is possible.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Bounded by the size of the current and previous sections.
*   **Neuron Data (250x230x90):** Uncompressed 5 MB becomes 1.1 MB (65,611 LBs), yielding a compression factor of ~4 (20% of original size).
*   **Cell Body Data (500x500x100):** Uncompressed 25 MB becomes 0.8 MB (50,218 LBs), yielding a compression factor of ~31 (3.2% of original size).
*   **Strengths:** Real-time processing, low memory footprint, efficient compression for filamentary data, easy incremental updates.
*   **Limitations:** Poor performance for short, blobby structures (cell bodies) compared to octrees; merging complexity; potential for false positives in reconstruction.
*   **When to use:** Filamentary volumetric data (neurons) from serial sectioning microscopy.
*   **When not to use:** Dense volumetric data or data with short, blobby structures where octrees may be more efficient.
